What: In GOautodial's goAPIv2 agent API, the goPhone request parameter is escaped for SQL (mysqli_real_escape_string) and then concatenated into an exec() command string. Shell metacharacters survive the SQL escape, so a $(...) payload runs on the host.
Impact: Any authenticated low-privilege agent — a role with no legitimate shell access — gets arbitrary OS command execution on the server running the API. CWE-78, CVSS 3.1 8.8 (High).
Fixed in: the installer-shipped goAPIv2 master branch (commit 0ab2584). Reported by me, Santosh Kumar Puppala — CVE requested/pending.

articles.author: Akhouri Anmol Kumar
articles.description:
Every time I needed to edit a screenshot, convert a HEIC file, compress an image for upload, — it was a different tool, a different tab, a different website with ads. So I built APIC (Advanced Image Processing Center) — one desktop app that handles the whole image workflow.
What's inside
APIC is built around five modules, all in one window:
Edit — crop, adjust, and touch up images without opening a browser tab
It also supports drag-and-drop straight onto the main window — drop one file and it opens in the editor, drop several and it routes you to the converter, which is the flow I actually wanted every time I used a tool like this before.
Why a desktop app instead of another web tool
Web-based image tools mean uploading your files to someone else's server, waiting on their upload/download cycle, and often hitting a paywall past the third free conversion. APIC runs locally — nothing leaves your machine, there's no queue, and it works offline.
Stack
Built with PyQt6 for the interface (dark theme, keyboard shortcuts for every major action), structured as separate mode modules so each part of the app — edit, convert, compress, search — is self-contained and easy to extend. Packaged as a standalone executable with PyInstaller.
Where it's headed
This is an early build. Batch processing across all four modules is next, along with more format support in Convert. If you work with images regularly and you're tired of the browser-tab shuffle, I'd genuinely like feedback on what's missing.
This is an Akhouri Systems product — same team behind ATLOCK, ACALCU, ANOTE.
https://akhouri-anmol-kumar.github.io/Akhouri-systems/
https://github.com/Akhouri-Anmol-Kumar/APIC
"We build what others forgot to fix."
articles.title: I got tired of having 5 different image tools open, so I built one that does everything

articles.author: Paris Moschovakos
articles.description:
Apple Mail keeps a full SQLite database of your mailbox metadata. It sits at
~/Library/Mail/V10/MailData/Envelope Index (the V number tracks the Mail
I spent the last months building an MCP server on top of this database, so here
The schema is normalized in an old-school, disciplined way. The tables you care
messages is the spine. One row per message across all accounts. It carries
date_sent, date_received,
read, flagged, deleted, a mailbox foreign key, a subject foreign key
sender foreign key. Note what it does not carry: the subject text and
subjects holds each distinct subject string exactly once. A thread of 40
messages pointing at one row
addresses does the same for people: one row per distinct address and
messages.sender.
recipients is the join table for To and Cc: message ROWID, address ROWID,
mailboxes maps mailbox ROWIDs to account and folder URLs. The URL encodes
attachments carries filename and MIME type per message, so "find the PDF
Message bodies. The Envelope Index is metadata only. Bodies live as individual
.emlx files next to the database, one file per message, named by ROWID. So
There is a second database next to it worth knowing about: the full text
Mail.app owns this database and holds it open with WAL journaling. The rules
Open read only, always: sqlite3.connect("file:...?mode=ro", uri=True).
Never write. Sends, flags and moves go through Mail itself, then you verify
by reading the database again.
Expect schema drift across macOS versions and feature-detect columns
instead of assuming them.
Full Disk Access is required. There is no way around it and that is
correct: this file is your entire mail history.
One number: a subject search across 300k messages that took 10 seconds through
The server that came out of this is open source (MIT):
https://github.com/parasxos/apple-mail-mcp
articles.title: What's actually inside Apple Mail's Envelope Index

articles.author: Zapp Chess
articles.description:
Zapp Chess skips the part of chess most people don't have time for. Every game starts from a curated middlegame position, so you're straight into tactics instead of building up an opening.
You're matched against real people, not bots. There's no opening theory to memorize — games are decided by tactics from the position you're given. A game ends when either side reaches a two-point material lead (pawn = 1, knight = 3, bishop = 3, rook = 5, queen = 9), or by checkmate. Games typically finish in about 3 minutes, and each move is played on your own time.

Since every game starts mid-position, there's nothing to memorize before you play. You just read the board and look for the best tactic.

You're paired with real opponents, not bots.

Because games are decided by a material lead or checkmate, there's no long endgame to play out.

Zapp Chess also has free web-based tools for studying afterward: /analysis, a Stockfish-powered board with PGN import and full game review, and /chess-clock, a set of clock presets.

Browser play is free — no download and no signup to start. An account is only needed if you want to save your progress. The apps are free on Android and iOS, and Zapp Chess is available in 16 languages.
Play now: https://zappchess.com

Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.zappchess.app.free

iOS: https://apps.apple.com/app/zapp-chess/id6759085538
articles.title: Zapp Chess: 3-Minute Chess Battles From the Middlegame
